title: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Eritrea: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Eritrea: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step serious and terminal illness checklist for Eritrea: palliative care coordination, advance directives, powers of attorney, disability and caregiver support, and estate preparation.
introHtml: Planning medical records, legal representation, civil identity documents, and benefits during a serious illness in Eritrea requires recognizing that Eritrea does not operate public online civil-status, court, or legislative gazette portals (state website shabait.com provides ministry news and policy statements only). Consequently, this guide cites verified international legal archives (FAOLEX, ILO NATLEX, Refworld, and HCCH) alongside accredited foreign consular guidance and Eritrean embassy portals, and families should verify current administrative steps directly with the relevant Zoba office or an Eritrean diplomatic mission.

steps.title: Request medical records and organize treatment and capacity documentation
steps.html:
• Ask the treating hospital or physician in Eritrea for signed clinical summaries, diagnostic records, medication lists, and capacity notes in Tigrigna, Arabic, or English so caregivers and designated representatives have clear documentation.
  • Clarify ongoing care preferences early with attending doctors and close relatives, as Eritrea has no public online advance-directive registry and legal duties of health professionals and personal representation fall under the Civil Code of Eritrea (2015) [1].

steps.title: Execute a consular or domestic Power of Attorney to authorize a local agent
steps.html:
• Because civil records, banking matters, and court applications in Eritrea cannot be completed online from abroad, appointing a trusted representative via a formal Power of Attorney (POA) is essential [8][9].
  • Inside Eritrea, execute the mandate before an authorized Public Notary in Asmara or the competent local office; outside Eritrea, the letter granting legal authority must be signed in person before an Eritrean consular officer [8].
  • Both the Embassy of the State of Eritrea in London and the Embassy of the State of Eritrea in Washington, D.C. require the principal to hold a valid Eritrean National ID card and provide the agent's full name, National ID number, and date of birth [8][9]; Washington D.C. applications run through CAPS online with specific fee tiers (USD 40 POA fee, USD 20 Asmara email fee, USD 10 service fee) plus current Recovery and Rehabilitation Tax clearance [9].

steps.title: Verify National ID, civil status entries, and Certificates of Existence
steps.html:
• Confirm that the patient's Eritrean National ID card, birth records, and passport details match municipal Public Registration Office and Zoba Administration files governed under the Civil Code of Eritrea (2015) and the Eritrean Nationality Proclamation No. 21/1992 [1][4][10].
  • Under consular ID rules, Eritreans aged 18 and older must maintain a valid Eritrean National ID card to request civil services or execute a Power of Attorney; lost or outdated cards require court authorization for any name or date-of-birth corrections [8][10].
  • If a pension payer or legal institution inside Eritrea requests proof that an Eritrean national residing abroad is alive, the individual can attend an Eritrean embassy in person with their National ID, proof of address, and photo to obtain a Certificate of Existence (Certificate of Life) [8].

steps.title: Review workplace sick-leave, disability, and social welfare entitlements
steps.html:
• Examine paid sick leave, medical incapacity termination protections, and employment injury benefits under Labour Proclamation No. 118/2001 [2].
  • Where a household qualifies for state welfare or disability/rehabilitation assistance, check eligibility criteria directly with the Ministry of Labor and Social Welfare, which also administers ongoing family allowances under Proclamation No. 137/2003 [6].
  • For Eritreans abroad needing a representative inside Eritrea to follow up on pension or benefit claims, verify dedicated consular POA options with the diplomatic mission [9].

steps.title: Prepare a valid will and follow non-Apostille consular authentication
steps.html:
• Draft a clear written or notarized will complying with Book 3 (Successions) of the Civil Code of Eritrea (2015) and procedural safeguards in the Civil Procedure Code (2015), noting that Zoba Courts and the High Court handle formal estate jurisdiction while Community Courts primarily mediate minor community disputes [1][3][7].
  • Verify cross-border document steps early because Eritrea is not a party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention [11].
  • Original Eritrean documents to be used abroad must first be authenticated by the Eritrean Ministry of Foreign Affairs in Asmara before presentation at a diplomatic mission, while foreign medical or legal records intended for use in Eritrea require prior authentication by the issuing country's Foreign Ministry (such as the U.S. Department of State or UK FCDO) before Eritrean embassy legalization [5][8].

contacts.name: Embassy of the State of Eritrea in Washington, D.C.
contacts.note: Processes online CAPS Power of Attorney applications, National ID renewals, and document legalization (1708 New Hampshire Ave NW).

contacts.name: Embassy of the State of Eritrea in London
contacts.note: Executes Powers of Attorney, issues Certificates of Existence (Certificate of Life), and authenticates legalized original documents by appointment.

contacts.name: Ministry of Labor and Social Welfare
contacts.note: Oversees national welfare, rehabilitation, and Martyrs' family support programs in Eritrea (in-country offices handle applications directly).
